transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm glad you're here. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'll be working—I'm a carpenter—and just one saw starting up in the shop, or somebody walking past the office, or even just a random thought about another job... it completely pulls me off what I’m doing. And then before I know it, the whole day just gets away from me.
Have you always had difficulty concentrating like this, even as far back as you can remember in childhood and school? Or is this something that's more recent?

No, it's definitely not recent. It's... well, it's been like this for as long as I can remember. Even way back in grade school, definitely before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mother the same thing. They'd say I was a bright kid but just careless. I was always losing my homework, or I'd completely forget the instructions they just gave the class. Instead of finishing my seatwork, I'd just be sitting there staring out the window. So, yeah, it's always been a problem for me.
When you're trying to focus on work or other tasks, do you find yourself needing to move around a lot, fidget with things, or feeling restless—like you just can't sit still?

Well, it's not so much that I'm running around the room, but... yeah, if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or if I'm stuck sitting through a long meeting, I definitely feel this... this restlessness. It's like I'm just wound up inside. I feel like I need to get up and move around. Even right now, I recently healed up a wrist injury and I know I'm supposed to just stay put and finish my paperwork, but it's really hard to just sit still and get it done.
Do you find yourself doing things without thinking them through first? For example, interrupting people, making quick decisions you later regret, or acting on impulse?

No, not really. I don't think I do that. I mean, I might zone out when someone's talking to me, but I don't interrupt them or talk over them. And as far as making quick decisions or doing things on impulse... no, I wouldn't say so. If anything, I just get sidetracked and forget to do things entirely. But I don't really have a problem with acting without thinking.

You mentioned feeling restless and wound up when you have to sit still. In a typical day, would you say you're generally more active or energetic than most people around you, or is it mainly just that sitting still feels uncomfortable?

I wouldn't say I'm more energetic than other people, no. It's really just the sitting still part that gets to me. When I'm working on a site, moving around, doing carpentry... I feel fine. But put me in a chair and tell me to stay there, and that's when I get that uncomfortable, restless feeling. So, no, I don't think I have more energy overall. I just don't like being stuck in one place.

When you were a kid in school, did your teachers or parents ever complain that you were too fidgety, restless, or hyperactive—like you couldn't sit still even during class or at the dinner table? Or was it mainly just the attention and focus problems they mentioned?

No, I don't remember anyone ever saying I was hyperactive or anything like that when I was a kid. It was always just about my focus. My teachers would tell my parents I was daydreaming or looking out the window, that I wasn't paying attention. But they never said I was running around the classroom or couldn't sit in my seat. It was always just that I was spaced out.

Looking back at your childhood and teenage years, did you ever have problems with impulsivity—like blurting things out, interrupting others, or doing things without thinking them through—even if you don't have those issues now?

No, I really don't think so. Even back then, I wasn't like that. I was more of a quiet kid who just... stared off into space, you know? I didn't blurt out answers or cut people off. Honestly, I was probably too busy being in my own head to interrupt anybody. So, no, I don't remember ever getting into trouble for doing things without thinking, even when I was younger.

When you were a child or teenager, did you ever have trouble waiting your turn, or did you find yourself acting before thinking things through—even if it wasn't as noticeable as daydreaming or not paying attention?

No, I don't remember having trouble waiting my turn or anything like that. Like I said, I was pretty quiet. I wasn't the type to jump the line or rush into things without thinking. I was mostly just... zoned out. So no, I didn't really have issues with acting before thinking, not that I can recall anyway.
